result.title: MegNIST, A Benchmark for Non-Invasive Inner Speech Decoding
result.summary: MegNIST is a benchmark dataset for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for inner speech decoding from magnetoencephalography (MEG). The dataset comprises 12,000 trials of a single participant imagining speaking the digits zero through nine, recorded across four sessions. Each trial contains 306-channel MEG recordings sampled at 250 Hz, preprocessed using signal space separation, filtering, and downsampling. Data are provided as pre-defined training (10,000 trials), validation (1,000 trials), and test (1,000 trials) splits, with entire experimental runs assigned to each split to preserve temporal independence. The dataset is available in both BIDS format for neuroimaging analysis and as serialised tensors for machine learning workflows. Baseline classification results demonstrate that imagined digits can be decoded significantly above chance. Standardised splits, validated baselines, example code, and a PyTorch-compatible loader in the pnpl Python library enable straightforward integration with machine learning frameworks, lowering barriers for researchers to rapidly develop and benchmark inner speech decoding methods for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建 MegNIST：单被试想象说出 0–9 数字的 306 通道 MEG 数据集（共 12,000 试次、四个 session），提供预处理数据、BIDS 与张量两种格式、按实验 run 划分的训练/验证/测试集，以及超过随机水平的基线分类与 PyTorch 加载器。
